answers.l: The first problem proven NP-complete, by Stephen Cook in 1971 and independently by Leonid Levin.
The Concorde solver found an optimal tour for an 85,900-city instance in 2006, yet no polynomial algorithm is known.
Only weakly NP-complete: a dynamic program solves it in O(nW) time, which is polynomial in the capacity's value but not its bit length.
One of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems from 1972; with only two literals per clause (2-SAT) it becomes solvable in linear time.
Taking both endpoints of a maximal matching gives a cover at most twice the optimal size, and no algorithm with a constant factor below 2 is known.
One of Karp's 21 problems from 1972; asking for a clique of size k is NP-complete when k is part of the input.
A set of vertices with no edges between them is exactly a clique in the complement graph, so the two problems reduce to each other.
One of Karp's 21 problems; it stays NP-complete even for planar cubic graphs (Garey, Johnson and Tarjan, 1976).
The Merkle-Hellman knapsack cryptosystem of 1978 was built on it, and Adi Shamir broke that scheme in 1982.
Deciding if a graph is 3-colorable is NP-complete, while 2-colorability is just a bipartiteness check.
The greedy algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of about ln n, and doing much better is NP-hard.
First-fit decreasing is a simple heuristic that never uses more than about 11/9 of the optimal number of bins.
Takayuki Yato and Takahiro Seta proved generalized n-by-n Sudoku NP-complete in 2003.
Splitting numbers into two equal-sum halves; Brian Hayes called it the easiest hard problem because a pseudo-polynomial DP often solves it.
Named for William Rowan Hamilton, whose 1857 Icosian game asked players to find such a route on a dodecahedron.
Donald Knuth's Algorithm X with Dancing Links solves it by backtracking, and Sudoku and pentomino tiling reduce to it.
Choose k vertices so every vertex is chosen or adjacent to a chosen one; it is a classic NP-complete problem listed by Garey and Johnson.
One of Karp's 21; unlike a minimum spanning tree it may add extra Steiner points to connect the required vertices more cheaply.
Remove the fewest vertices so the graph has no cycles; Karp listed it as feedback node set in 1972.
Goemans and Williamson's 1995 semidefinite programming algorithm approximates it within about 0.878 of optimal.
One of Karp's 21; the two-dimensional version is ordinary bipartite matching and solvable in polynomial time.
Jobs with fixed machine orders must be scheduled to meet a makespan bound; a famous 10x10 benchmark from 1963 stayed unsolved until 1989.
Karp listed 0-1 integer programming among his 21 problems, while linear programming without integrality is solvable in polynomial time.
Asking whether some input makes a Boolean circuit output true; textbooks often use it as the first NP-complete problem via the Cook-Levin proof.
Richard Kaye showed in 2000 that checking whether a Minesweeper board is consistent is NP-complete.
Demaine, Hohenberger and Liben-Nowell proved offline Tetris NP-complete, publishing as Tetris is Hard, Even to Approximate.
NP-complete in general graphs, yet solvable in linear time on a DAG using a topological order.
One of Karp's 21: pick k pairwise disjoint sets from a family. It contains independent set as a special case.
One of Karp's 21; it is set cover with the roles of elements and sets swapped.
Stephen Cook's 1971 paper used it as an example of an NP-complete problem, alongside SAT.
Gregory Chaitin's 1981 allocator modeled registers as colors on an interference graph, so optimal allocation inherits coloring's hardness.
Splitting a graph into equal halves with few crossing edges, also called minimum bisection; tools like METIS use heuristics for it.
Arnborg, Corneil and Proskurowski showed in 1987 that deciding treewidth at most k is NP-complete when k is part of the input.
Assigning jobs to m identical machines to meet a makespan bound; Graham's 1966 list scheduling gives a simple 2-approximation.
Introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959 for gasoline delivery trucks; it generalizes the traveling salesman problem.
Posed by Koopmans and Beckmann in 1957 for placing facilities; Sahni and Gonzalez showed even approximating it is NP-hard.
One of Karp's 21: remove the fewest edges to make a directed graph acyclic. It shows up when ranking from inconsistent pairwise votes.
One of Karp's 21: partition the vertices into k cliques, which is the same as coloring the complement graph.
For two strings it follows from the LCS dynamic program; for many strings David Maier showed it NP-complete in 1978.
Two strings are handled by the classic diff-style DP, but with an arbitrary number of strings Maier proved it NP-complete in 1978.
Toby Walsh showed in 2014 that generalized Candy Crush is NP-hard by reducing 3-SAT to it.

answers.n: Rubik's Cube (optimal n x n x n)
answers.l: In 2018 Erik Demaine and colleagues proved that finding the shortest solution for a generalized n x n x n cube is NP-complete.
Installability of Debian packages was shown NP-complete by the EDOS project in 2006, and Russ Cox revisited it in his 2016 essay Version SAT.
Even, Itai and Shamir proved timetable construction NP-complete in 1976; exam scheduling is graph coloring in disguise.
Ueda and Nagao proved in 1996 that deciding whether a nonogram has a solution is NP-complete.
Each clause needs at least one true and one false literal; Thomas Schaefer proved it NP-complete in his 1978 dichotomy theorem.
Each clause must have exactly one true literal; Schaefer showed it stays NP-complete even with no negated literals.
2-SAT is easy, but satisfying at least k of the 2-literal clauses is NP-complete (Garey, Johnson and Stockmeyer, 1976).
David Lichtenstein proved in 1982 that 3-SAT stays NP-complete when its variable-clause graph is planar, a workhorse for puzzle hardness proofs.
Strongly NP-complete, so unlike plain partition it stays hard even when the numbers are written in unary (Garey and Johnson, 1975).
Ian Holyer showed in 1981 that deciding if a cubic graph needs 3 or 4 colors for its edges is NP-complete, even though Vizing bounds it.
Generalized Kakuro, the cross-sum puzzle, was shown NP-complete by Takahiro Seta in 2002.
Order the vertices so adjacent ones sit close together; Papadimitriou proved it NP-complete in 1976, and it matters for banded sparse matrices.
Deciding if pathwidth is at most k is NP-complete; it equals the vertex separation number from layout problems.
Garey and Johnson proved in 1983 that finding the minimum number of edge crossings in a drawing is NP-complete.
Carsten Thomassen proved in 1989 that deciding whether a graph embeds on a surface of genus k is NP-complete.
Find the largest graph contained in two given graphs; it generalizes subgraph isomorphism and is used to compare chemical structures.
Asking for an induced copy of a pattern graph; with a path as pattern it becomes the longest induced path problem.
Equivalent to minimum maximal matching; Yannakakis and Gavril proved it NP-complete in 1980.
Finding a small one is equivalent to finding a spanning tree with many leaves, and it is used to build routing backbones in wireless networks.
Asking for a spanning tree with max degree 2 is the Hamiltonian path problem, so the general version is NP-complete.
Hell and Nesetril proved in 1990 that H-coloring is NP-complete unless H is bipartite or has a loop.
The shortest string containing every input as a substring; Gallant, Maier and Storer proved it NP-complete in 1980, and it models genome assembly.
Find a string within Hamming distance d of every input string; Frances and Litman proved it NP-complete in 1997.
Post's correspondence problem is undecidable, but asking for a solution of at most k tiles is NP-complete.
Wang and Jiang proved in 1994 that optimal sum-of-pairs alignment of many sequences is NP-complete, so tools like Clustal use heuristics.
Building the phylogenetic tree with the fewest evolutionary changes was proven NP-complete by Foulds and Graham in 1982.
Assign jobs to agents with capacity limits at minimum cost; it contains bin packing and knapsack as special cases.
Gonzalez and Sahni showed in 1976 that it is polynomial for two machines but NP-complete for three or more.
Johnson's rule solves two machines optimally, but minimizing makespan with three machines is NP-hard (Garey, Johnson and Sethi, 1976).
Choosing revenue-maximizing winning bids on bundles is weighted set packing, so it is NP-complete.
Peter van Emde Boas proved it NP-complete in 1981; lattice cryptography relies on its hardness.
Color elements red and blue so no set is monochromatic, also called hypergraph 2-coloring or Property B.
Garey and Johnson proved in 1977 that connecting points with horizontal and vertical wire of minimum length is NP-complete, which matters for chip routing.
A simple greedy algorithm gives a 2-approximation, and doing better is NP-hard.
Choosing which warehouses to open to minimize opening plus service costs; the uncapacitated version is NP-hard by reduction from set cover.
Ratner and Warmuth proved in 1986 that finding the shortest solution of the generalized n x n sliding puzzle is NP-complete.
Stuckman and Zhang proved in 2006 that deciding whether a set of guesses and responses has any consistent secret code is NP-complete.
Malte Helmert proved in 2003 that deciding whether a generalized FreeCell deal is solvable is NP-complete.
Uehara and Iwata proved generalized peg solitaire NP-complete in 1990.
Takayuki Yato proved this Nikoli loop puzzle NP-complete in 2000.
Brandon McPhail proved the Nikoli puzzle Light Up, also called Akari, NP-complete in 2005.
Holzer, Klein and Kutz published a proof that the Nurikabe pencil puzzle is NP-complete in 2004.
Merlijn Sevenster proved in 2004 that solving solitaire Battleship from row and column counts is NP-complete.
Bill Gates co-wrote a 1979 paper bounding it, and Bulteau, Fertin and Rusu later proved finding the minimum flips NP-hard.
Mihalis Yannakakis proved in 1981 that adding the fewest edges to make a graph chordal is NP-complete, which matters for sparse Cholesky factorization.
Measures how many insertions, deletions and relabelings turn one graph into another; it generalizes subgraph isomorphism, so it is NP-hard.
Bansal, Blum and Chawla introduced it in 2002 and showed that clustering to minimize disagreements with similarity labels is NP-complete.
Covering every edge is the polynomial Chinese postman problem, but covering only a required subset is NP-complete (Lenstra and Rinnooy Kan, 1976).
Add the fewest edges to make a graph Hamiltonian; the answer is zero exactly when it already has a Hamiltonian cycle.
Every planar graph is 4-colorable, but deciding 3-colorability stays NP-complete even with max degree 4 (Garey, Johnson, Stockmeyer, 1976).
Hyafil and Rivest proved in 1976 that building a binary decision tree with minimum expected tests is NP-complete; practical learners like ID3 and CART build trees greedily.
Partition the vertices into as many disjoint dominating sets as possible; even deciding whether three exist is NP-complete.
The most colors in a proper coloring where every pair of colors meets on some edge; Yannakakis and Gavril proved it NP-complete in 1980.
Can the edges be 2-colored so that no triangle is all one color? It appears in Garey and Johnson's 1979 list of NP-complete problems.
The fewest bicliques needed to cover all edges; James Orlin proved computing it NP-complete in 1977.
The smallest set of landmark vertices whose distances identify every vertex uniquely; Garey and Johnson listed it as NP-complete.
The fewest dimensions needed to represent a graph as intersecting axis-parallel boxes; Kratochvil showed even boxicity 2 is NP-complete in 1994.
Lay vertices on a line to minimize the most edges crossing any gap; it is NP-complete and appears in Garey and Johnson's list.
The fewest planar layers needed to draw a graph's edges; Anthony Mansfield proved in 1983 that deciding thickness 2 is NP-hard.
The fewest pages needed in a book embedding; testing whether two pages suffice is NP-complete because it relates to Hamiltonian cycles in planar graphs.
Fellows, Rosamond, Rotics and Szeider proved in 2009 that computing clique-width is NP-complete.
Coloring vertices and edges together; Sanchez-Arroyo proved deciding the total chromatic number NP-complete in 1989.
Each vertex must take a color from its own allowed list; it generalizes ordinary coloring, so it is NP-complete.
The most colors greedy coloring can be forced to use over all vertex orders; computing it is NP-complete.
Fractional multicommodity flow is solvable by linear programming, but Even, Itai and Shamir showed integral flow with two commodities is NP-complete.
Connecting k source-sink pairs with disjoint paths is NP-complete when k is part of the input, but Robertson and Seymour solved fixed k in polynomial time.
Folding a chain in the hydrophobic-polar lattice model was proved NP-complete in 1998 by Berger and Leighton and by Crescenzi and colleagues.
E. Mark Gold proved in 1978 that finding the smallest automaton consistent with labeled example strings is NP-complete.
Finding the smallest context-free grammar that generates exactly one given string is NP-hard; compressors like Sequitur approximate it.
Johan Hastad proved in 1990 that computing the rank of a 3-dimensional tensor over a finite field is NP-complete, while matrix rank is easy.
Finding the fewest columns whose combination fits a target vector is NP-hard (Natarajan, 1995); compressed sensing uses L1 relaxation instead.
Blum and Rivest proved in 1988 that training even a 3-node neural network to fit given data is NP-complete.
David Maxwell Chickering proved in 1996 that learning the best-scoring Bayesian network structure is NP-complete.
Abraham, Blum and Sandholm showed in 2007 that clearing a kidney exchange with cycle length capped at 3 is NP-complete; length 2 is just matching.
Alberto Caprara proved the unsigned version NP-hard in 1997, while Hannenhalli and Pevzner solved the signed version in polynomial time.
In this Nikoli puzzle, islands are joined by bridges; deciding whether a puzzle has a solution is NP-complete.
Erich Friedman proved this Nikoli pearl loop puzzle NP-complete in 2002.
Holzer and Ruepp proved this Nikoli room-shading puzzle NP-complete in 2007.
Shading duplicate numbers so the rest stays connected is NP-complete for generalized Hitori boards.
Takayuki Yato showed this Nikoli polyomino-filling puzzle NP-complete.
Markus Holzer and Waltraud Holzer proved in 2004 that the generalized Tantrix rotation puzzle is NP-complete.
Erik and Martin Demaine proved it NP-complete in 2007; the Eternity II edge-matching puzzle offered a 2 million dollar prize that nobody claimed.
Filling a grid with words from a given list is NP-complete and appears in Garey and Johnson's 1979 list.
Clifford, Jalsenius, Montanaro and Sach proved in 2012 that finding the fewest moves in the Flood-It game is NP-hard.
Longpre and McKenzie proved that Thoughtful Klondike, played with every card visible, is NP-complete.
With every tile position known in advance, deciding whether a layout can be fully cleared is NP-complete.
Biedl and colleagues proved in 2002 that clearing a SameGame-style Clickomania board is NP-complete, even with only two columns.
The 1960s four-cube stacking puzzle; Robertson and Munro proved the generalized n-cube version NP-complete in 1978.
Berlekamp, McEliece and van Tilborg proved in 1978 that maximum-likelihood decoding of a general linear code is NP-complete.

answers.n: Minimum distance of a linear code
answers.l: Alexander Vardy proved in 1997 that computing the minimum distance of a binary linear code is NP-hard, settling a question open since 1978.
Francisco Barahona proved in 1982 that finding ground states of 3D Ising spin glasses is NP-hard, while the planar case is polynomial.
Delete the fewest vertices to make a graph bipartite; it is NP-complete under Yannakakis's general node-deletion results.
Add or delete the fewest edges to turn a graph into disjoint cliques; Krivanek and Moravek proved it NP-hard in 1986.
Manders and Adleman proved in 1978 that deciding if ax^2 + by = c has positive integer solutions is NP-complete.
Finding k vertices with the most edges among them generalizes the clique problem, so it is NP-complete.
Splitting the vertices into disjoint triangles is NP-complete and is a common stepping stone in reductions from 3-dimensional matching.
Keeping the fewest edges with the same reachability is NP-complete, since a strong digraph has an n-edge one exactly when it has a Hamiltonian cycle.
Choose the fewest tests that tell every pair of items apart; Garey and Johnson list it, and it models fault diagnosis.
Extending a partial coloring is NP-complete even on interval graphs, where ordinary coloring is easy (Biro, Hujter and Tuza, 1992).
Finding the cheapest tree spanning exactly k vertices is NP-hard, unlike the ordinary minimum spanning tree.
Bulteau, Fertin and Rusu proved in 2012 that computing the transposition distance between permutations is NP-hard, settling a long-open genome rearrangement question.
Aho, Johnson and Ullman proved in 1977 that optimal code for expressions with common subexpressions is NP-complete, while expression trees are easy.
Tiling a finite square with given Wang tiles is NP-complete, while tiling the whole plane is undecidable (Berger, 1966).
Find an integer avoiding a list of residues modulo given numbers; Garey and Johnson list it as NP-complete in number theory.
Also called minimum maximal independent set; finding any maximal independent set is easy, but finding the smallest one is NP-hard.
An independent set that every outside vertex points into; Vasek Chvatal proved in 1973 that deciding if a digraph has one is NP-complete.

answers.n: Sequencing with release times and deadlines
answers.l: Scheduling jobs on one machine within release times and deadlines is strongly NP-complete, problem SS1 in Garey and Johnson.

answers.l: Find a path that never uses both vertices of a forbidden pair; Gabow, Maheshwari and Osterweil proved it NP-complete in 1976 while studying program testing.

nope.Halting problem: Undecidable, so it is not in NP at all.
nope.Graph isomorphism: In NP but not known to be NP-complete; Babai gave a quasipolynomial algorithm in 2015.
nope.Integer factorization: Its decision version is in NP and co-NP, so it is not believed to be NP-complete.
nope.2-SAT: Solvable in linear time via strongly connected components.
nope.Shortest path: Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford solve it in polynomial time.
nope.Linear programming: Solvable in polynomial time by the ellipsoid and interior-point methods.
nope.Primality testing: In P since the AKS algorithm of 2002.
nope.Chess: Generalized chess is EXPTIME-complete, which is harder than NP.
nope.Go: Generalized Go with Japanese ko rules is EXPTIME-complete.
nope.Sokoban: PSPACE-complete, not known to be in NP.
nope.Super Mario Bros: Generalized Super Mario Bros was proven PSPACE-complete in 2016.
nope.Nash equilibrium: Finding one is PPAD-complete, a different class.
nope.Chinese postman problem: Solvable in polynomial time with matching.
nope.Eulerian path: Checkable in linear time by vertex degrees.
nope.Lights Out: Solvable in polynomial time with linear algebra over GF(2).
nope.Tower of Hanoi: The optimal solution is known exactly; it is not NP-complete.
nope.QBF: True quantified Boolean formulas are PSPACE-complete.

traps.q: Which problem did Stephen Cook prove NP-complete in 1971, making it the first one?
traps.l: Cook's paper The Complexity of Theorem-Proving Procedures introduced NP-completeness, and Leonid Levin proved a similar result independently.

traps.q: Which NP-complete problem had an 85,900-city instance solved to proven optimality by the Concorde solver in 2006?
traps.l: The instance came from a chip layout application, and solving it took Concorde the equivalent of many CPU years.
